election._note: Elected 3-4 October 2025 for a four-year term, so the next falls in October 2028; no fixed date announced. The real system runs d'Hondt over a single national constituency with a 5% bar for single parties and higher effective bars for coalitions; the machinery's plain d'Hondt carries the shape. Wikipedia, 'Next Czech legislative election'.

dissolution._note: Art. 35: the President may dissolve the Chamber where a newly appointed government loses confidence, where the Chamber fails to decide on confidence within three months, or where it adjourns itself beyond 120 days -- the machinery's confidence_failure, reachable only through a lost vote. Since the 2009 amendment the power cannot be used in the last three months of the term; shortening the term then needs a constitutional act, which is what the Chamber did to itself that year -- and the Constitutional Court annulled the first attempt. Elections follow within 60 days, the two-month notice. Ustava, Arts. 31 and 35.

upper._note: Senate, 81 seats, one third elected every two years in two-round constituency contests. Ordinary: the Senate may reject or amend and the Chamber overrides by an absolute majority of all deputies (Art. 46) -- suspensive. The amendment row is ALSO suspensive, which is a REDUCTION and is recorded as one: constitutional acts require both chambers to pass the same text with a 3/5 majority each (Art. 39(4)), so the Senate cannot be overridden there at all -- the mirror of AUT.json's reduction, authored as fixed because this model has no joint-sitting machinery to carry the real rule. Ustava, Arts. 39, 46, 106.

head_of_state._note: The President, directly elected for five years by two-round vote; last elected January 2023, so the next falls in January 2028. Mostly ceremonial but with a veto, the appointment role and the Art. 35 dissolution triggers. Wikipedia, 'President of the Czech Republic'.
head_of_state.title: President

amendment._note: Art. 39(4): a constitutional act needs a 3/5 majority of all deputies and a 3/5 majority of senators present. The machinery carries no three_fifths in this template, so the rule reads two_thirds -- the nearest stricter reading, SVK.json's own resolution, and the difference only matters for amendment content this game prices by support, not by threshold. Ustava, Art. 39(4).
amendment._permits_system_change_note: Art. 9(2): any change in the essential requirements of a democratic state governed by the rule of law is impermissible -- a written restraint on revising the system itself, and the Constitutional Court's 2009 Plenum judgment is the operative precedent for enforcing it. Thinner than Germany's Art. 79(3) identity clause; flagged as such rather than asserted with equal confidence.

judicial._note: Ustavni soud, Art. 87: strikes down laws or their parts contrary to the constitutional order; the 2009 judgment annulling the constitutional act that shortened the Chamber's term is the case the dissolution note above turns on. Ustava, Art. 87.

formation._note: The President appoints the Prime Minister, who presents the Government to the Chamber for a confidence vote within 30 days of appointment -- an investiture in the machinery's vocabulary. Censure carries by an absolute majority of all deputies on a written motion of fifty (Art. 72); the template's permitted readings are simple_present and the German-style constructive rule, so simple_present ships with the absolute-of-all reality recorded rather than detuned -- SVK.json's tolerance. Ustava, Arts. 68, 72, 75.

government._pretender_note: Whom data/laws/amendments.json's Restoration Act puts on the throne. Authored per nation because the law is generic and the dynasty is not; a monarchy points this at its own sitting monarch.

fiscal._note: General government, IMF/OECD estimates ~2024, rounded, on the same conventions as SVK.json's block. VAT 21% and corporate 21% are the statutory rates; income 17 is a blend of the 15/23 progressive schedule; capital gains 15% is the schedule's base rate (23% above the threshold). Debt ~42.6% and revenue ~33.5% of GDP (Eurostat/OECD 2024). Spending is the general-government split scaled to expenditure near 46.5% of GDP.
